speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're listening to Scaling DevTools.
zh: 你正在收听的是 Scaling DevTools。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm joined today by Dennis from Unblocked.
zh: 今天和我一起的是来自 Unblocked 的 Dennis。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, thanks so much for having me.
zh: 你好，非常感谢邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to catch up in person.
zh: 很高兴能当面聊聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so it's the second time that you've been on, but yeah, this time we have a grand piano in our background.
zh: 是的，这是你第二次上节目了，不过这次我们的背景里有一架三角钢琴。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're looking for a place to sit, and we can only find one beside a grand piano.
zh: 我们在找地方坐，结果只能在三角钢琴旁边找到一个位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not too bad.
zh: 那也不算太糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're at LeadDev, so I should thank you, LeadDev, for having me, allowing me to do this.
zh: 我们现在在 LeadDev,所以我应该感谢你,LeadDev,邀请我来,让我能做这期节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: How have you been finding the conference so far?
zh: 到目前为止你觉得这个大会怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's phenomenal.
zh: 非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's one of my favorite conferences this year, for sure.
zh: 我觉得这肯定是我今年最喜欢的大会之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been to a couple that I really enjoyed, but the level of talks, the organization of the event, the people, it's fantastic.
zh: 我们参加过几个我很喜欢的大会，但这里的演讲水平、活动的组织、参会的人，都太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's just like, yeah, it's definitely a highlight.
zh: 我觉得就是，对，这绝对是一个亮点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with the only addition next time that you're going to bolt on some surfing.
zh: 而且唯一需要补充的是，下次你要顺便加上海上冲浪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hopefully.
zh: 希望如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, we were chatting about surfing.
zh: 是的，我们刚才在聊冲浪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to maybe add a day on either end of the trip to see if I can get some surfing in the UK for sure.
zh: 我很想在行程的两端各加一天，看看能不能在英国冲上一次浪，这是肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd love that.
zh: 我们很乐见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is very good.
zh: 这非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone listening should go surf in the UK.
zh: 所有听众都应该去英国冲浪。

speaker: Unknown
en: For sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bring your wetsuit.
zh: 带上你的潜水服。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bring your wetsuit.
zh: 带上你的潜水服。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bring a fake one.
zh: 带一件假的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So could you tell us, I know you've been on kind of a journey since we last spoke, could you tell us a bit about Unblocked and what...
zh: 那你能给我们讲讲吗，我记得上次我们聊完之后你经历了一段旅程，你能讲讲 Unblocked 以及什么……

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's been a crazy, I don't know, probably six to eight months, 10 months or so.
zh: 我是说，这大概是疯狂的四……不知道，大概六到八个月，十个月左右吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unblocked originally started as a platform.
zh: Unblocked 最初是一个平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, let's take a step even way further back.
zh: 好吧，我们再往回退得更远一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Up until six to eight months ago, people were the beings that actually went and wrote code, right?
zh: 直到六到八个月前，人类还是真正去写代码的存在，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in order for them to be able to write code in their business, in their organizations, they needed a bunch of context.
zh: 为了让他们能在自己的业务、自己的组织里写代码，他们需要大量的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Unblocked has always been this context layer that had interfaces where people could ask questions and get answers.
zh: 所以 Unblocked 一直是这个上下文层，它有各种界面，让人们可以提问并获得答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eight months ago, six months ago, thereabouts, towards the end of late last year, I would say, we saw that it was increasingly these agentic workflows that were becoming quite popular.
zh: 八个月前，六个月前，差不多那个时候，大概在去年年底，我们看到智能体工作流越来越流行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was increasingly agents writing code instead of people.
zh: 而且越来越多地是智能体在写代码，而不是人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so people were helping that process, but agents needed the same level of context that people had and didn't have it available to them.
zh: 人们在辅助这个过程，但智能体需要和人类同等水平的上下文，却没有可用的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've been focusing on making agents just far, far better with servicing that context layer and making it available to them.
zh: 所以我们一直专注于让智能体借助这个上下文层的服务变得远远更好，并让上下文对它们可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we're seeing is agents are getting their jobs, their tasks done between 40% to 60% faster with Unblocked.
zh: 所以我们看到的是，有了 Unblocked,智能体完成工作、完成任务的速度提高了 40% 到 60%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're seeing significant token savings, anywhere between 30% to 50% less token usage for a given task.
zh: 而且我们看到显著的 token 节省，对于一个给定任务，token 用量减少 30% 到 50% 不等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, that's a little bit what we've been thinking about.
zh: 所以，对，这就是我们一直在思考的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like with, I guess context is like a big topic.
zh: 而，我想上下文是个很大的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the parts that like, are there any interesting things that you've like discovered about like what really matters in terms of context?
zh: 有哪些部分，就是你有没有发现什么有意思的事情，关于在上下文方面什么才是真正重要的？

speaker: Unknown
en: For sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like this expression when it's old is new again.
zh: 我喜欢这句话：旧即是新。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about your first day at a company, you had no idea how the code base worked or why it worked the way it did or how decisions get made or any of that information.
zh: 想想你在一家公司的第一天,你完全不知道代码库是怎么运作的,也不知道它为什么会以这种方式运作,不知道决策是怎么做出的,也不知道任何这类信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: In some capacity, you had to build all this context as a consequence of digging through information or interrupting your coworkers, opening pull requests, getting feedback on your code.
zh: 在某种程度上,你必须通过翻查信息、打断同事、开 pull request、获得对你代码的反馈,才能逐渐建立起所有这些上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Participating in post-mortems for outages hopefully you didn't cause, but maybe you did, right?
zh: 参与故障复盘(post-mortem),希望不是你造成的,但也可能是你造成的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: These are all the lessons and the context that you built as a consequence.
zh: 这些都是你由此积累起来的经验和上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so over time, you've gotten to be really good at your job because you have all that context.
zh: 所以随着时间推移,你变得非常擅长你的工作,因为你拥有了所有那些上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all of that information is what is missing when an agent gets spawned in a terminal.
zh: 而所有这些信息,恰恰是一个智能体在终端里被生成时所缺失的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time you spin a new agent up, it's like you on day one at that company.
zh: 每次你启动一个新智能体,它就像你在这家公司的第一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has no idea about how these things work.
zh: 它完全不知道这些东西是怎么运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what it does is struggle.
zh: 所以它做的就是挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does a bunch of unnecessary tool calling or grepping through the source code.
zh: 它会做一堆不必要的工具调用,或者在源代码里 grep 来 grep 去。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has a whole bunch of limitations in the way that it's trying to get the information it needs in order to get its job done.
zh: 它在试图获取完成工作所需信息的方式上,存在一大堆局限。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the mental model that I think about, which is you open a new Claude Code terminal, what does it know about your organization?
zh: 这就是我所想的思维模型,也就是:你打开一个新的 Claude Code 终端,它对你的组织了解多少?

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing.
zh: 一无所知。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has to learn it all again.
zh: 它必须把所有东西重新学一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see people go through these phases of spoon-feeding a context to get them up to speed, basically.
zh: 我们看到人们经历这些阶段,基本上就是手动喂上下文,让它们跟上进度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's, I guess like the challenge that I saw working with Context was like, we would try to, trying to decide like what, cause we were, we were building something that like used Context and they had to know about their business and stuff like that.
zh: 我想,就像我在做 Context 相关工作时看到的挑战是,我们得去决定……因为我们当时在做一个使用 Context 的东西,而它必须了解他们的业务之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would be like,
zh: 情况会是这样:

speaker: Unknown
en: Things would kind of contradict each other sometimes and like it was like trying to do like help keep memory of like okay this thing happened but maybe that information becomes out of date and like so do you keep it around but then you're deciding like which things are still relevant and like how these kind of things are.
zh: 这些东西有时候会互相矛盾,就像要帮它保持记忆,比如说好吧这件事发生了,但也许那个信息会过时,那你要不要保留它?然后你就得决定哪些东西仍然相关,以及这类事情该怎么处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's been super interesting over the last probably year or so, seeing how organizations adopt AI, agentic coding specifically, AI for their agentic coding scenarios.
zh: 你知道,在过去大概一年左右的时间里,看到各组织如何采用 AI,具体说是智能体编程(agentic coding),AI 用于他们的智能体编程场景,一直非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we've found is basically there's kind of a maturity model, right?
zh: 我们发现的基本上是一种成熟度模型(maturity model),对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because different organizations do it at different rates, and even within the organizations, different people do it at different rates.
zh: 因为不同组织采用的速度不同,即使在同一个组织内部,不同的人采用的速度也不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the most like nascent version of that maturity model, I think it largely stems from people using Obsidian or like collecting a bunch of files that they have locally that helps those agents understand how they should perform.
zh: 在这个成熟度模型最初始的阶段,我认为它主要源于人们使用 Obsidian,或者在本地收集一堆文件,来帮助那些智能体理解他们应该怎么执行任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's everyone's like, yeah, I can totally recognize that.
zh: 我觉得每个人都会说,是的,我完全能认出这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at some point they like sit down and work with someone else and they're like, well, is this how I think about context?
zh: 然后在某个时候,他们坐下来和别人一起工作,然后说,嗯,这是我对上下文的思考方式吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how you think about it.
zh: 你是这样思考的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we have to like merge these two things together.
zh: 所以现在我们得把这两者合并起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're hand curating this context and you check that in probably and it is now basically a static data source, right?
zh: 于是你在手工策展(curate)这些上下文,你大概会把它 check in 进去,现在它基本上就是一个静态数据源了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a static chunk of information that you have to now manage and maintain.
zh: 它是一块静态的信息,你现在必须去管理和维护它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everyone's had some experience with Confluence at some point or any kind of wiki or document.
zh: 我想每个人都曾在某个时候用过 Confluence,或者任何类型的 wiki 或文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: Moments after you're finished writing the document, it's obsolete, right?
zh: 你写完文档的那一刻起,它就过时了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then you have to find someone to manage that.
zh: 所以接下来你就得找某个人来管理它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at a sufficiently scaled organization, finding someone who can apply the judgment that makes sense for their entire organization is actually really hard.
zh: 而在一个规模足够大的组织里,找到一个能够对整个组织做出合理判断的人,实际上非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this idea of hand-curating context gets you a level up in terms of the agent's ability to do their work, but you kind of hit a ceiling.
zh: 所以这种手工策展上下文的做法,能让智能体的工作能力提升一个层级,但你基本上会撞到天花板。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people are like, well, I have the static data source.
zh: 于是人们会说,好吧,我有这个静态数据源。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most natural thing to do is now surface the context through MCP.
zh: 最自然的做法就是现在通过 MCP 把这个上下文呈现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like the next kind of stage is like I'm going to expose all of my line of business systems to these MCP servers.
zh: 所以下一个阶段就像:我要把我所有的业务系统都暴露给这些 MCP 服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that, again, provides you a level up.
zh: 嗯,这又让你提升了一个层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: What ends up happening is that the agents don't know how to think about data across a whole bunch of different services.
zh: 但最终发生的情况是,智能体不知道如何在横跨一大堆不同服务的数据之间进行思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this term that we've really found a great way of describing.
zh: 有一个术语,我们觉得它描述得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called satisfaction of search.
zh: 它叫「搜索满足感」(satisfaction of search)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Its origin was actually from radiology.
zh: 它实际上起源于放射学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's basically the phenomenon where radiologists would unconsciously dismiss
zh: 它基本上是这样一种现象:放射科医生一旦发现了第一个异常,

speaker: Unknown
en: Any potential other anomalies once they found the first one, right?
zh: 就会无意识地忽略任何其他潜在的异常,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So like think about it as a patient, you would not want your radiologist being like, oh, that's it, we're done, let's move on.
zh: 想象你是病人,你肯定不希望你的放射科医生说,哦,就是它了,我们完了,继续下一步吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want an exhaustive search through all the imaging to make sure that like they've identified everything that's required for them to come to a complete conclusion.
zh: 你希望他们对所有影像做穷尽式的检查,以确保他们识别出了得出完整结论所需的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents do the exact same thing.
zh: 智能体会做出完全一样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll hit the Notion MCP, they'll hit the Slack MCP, they find something that looks right, and they carry on their merry way.
zh: 它们会查一下 Notion 的 MCP,查一下 Slack 的 MCP,找到某个看起来对的东西,然后就心满意足地继续走下去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't go to the exercise of making sure that it's actually fully correct and finding information that actually might change that conclusion.
zh: 而且不会去做那种确认它是否真正完全正确的功课，也不会去寻找可能改变那个结论的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So like MCP is a great enabler to help you get rid of this kind of content rot that happens when you hand curate this stuff.
zh: 所以 MCP 是一个很好的助推器，能帮你摆脱这种当你手工策展这些内容时产生的内容腐烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, it doesn't give you the exhaustive truth.
zh: 但再说一次，它并不能给你穷尽的真相。

speaker: Unknown
en: There isn't like a fully reconciled view of the thing that the agent is looking for because it's only finding in one data source.
zh: 对于智能体正在寻找的东西，并没有一个完全核对过的视图，因为它只在一个数据源里查找。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then the next final stage is basically building a content layer, right?
zh: 那么下一个最终阶段基本上就是构建一个内容层，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or a context layer, I should say.
zh: 或者说，我应该说是上下文层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's basically the idea of pulling all that information together, creating a knowledge graph, and then making it accessible for agents to call into and get answers right away, right?
zh: 这基本上就是把所有那些信息拉到一起、创建一个知识图谱，然后让它可以被智能体调用并立刻得到答案的想法，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: They're completely reconciled across all these different data sources across your entire team.
zh: 它们在你整个团队的所有这些不同数据源之间是完全核对过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, this seems really valuable because I remember some of the challenges we had was like time, like time-based information where it's like a superseded out of time and then also stuff like, I always thought, this is an interesting one, I asked it like, tell me Jack Bridger's secrets and it would just like,
zh: 是的，这看起来真的很有价值，因为我记得我们遇到的一些挑战是基于时间的，就是基于时间的信息，比如某个东西过时被取代了，还有比如——我一直觉得这个很有意思——我问它“告诉我 Jack Bridger 的秘密”，它就会直接——

speaker: Unknown
en: It would just use a search, this is not a context necessary, but it would use a search tool to search Jack Bridger's secrets.
zh: 它就会直接用一个搜索，这不是上下文必须的，但它会用一个搜索工具去搜索“Jack Bridger 的秘密”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was like, oh, I can't find any.
zh: 然后它就说，哦,我找不到任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, well, if you were a human tasked with that, you'd be like, hmm, I don't know, how could I uncover this guy's secrets?
zh: 然后你会想，如果你是一个被委派这个任务的人类，你会想，嗯,我不知道,我怎么才能挖掘出这家伙的秘密?

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'll listen to the podcast transcripts to find.
zh: 也许我会去听播客转写稿来找找。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it would just do dumb search terms or something.
zh: 但它只会做一些愚蠢的搜索词之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this the kind of things that you guys are sort of… The agents are like phenomenal at writing code, right?
zh: 这是你们在做的这类事情吗……智能体在写代码方面是现象级的，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But they don't understand necessarily a lot of the intent behind the code that they write.
zh: 但它们不一定理解它们所写的代码背后的很多意图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's often misconstrued, right?
zh: 所以经常被误解，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, these… I think of them as like expert strangers, right?
zh: 所以,你知道,这些……我把它们想象成像是陌生的专家，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: This other kind of…
zh: 这另一种……

speaker: Unknown
en: Mental Model that I have is imagine you have two people who have 10 years of experience.
zh: 我有的一个心智模型是，想象你有两个有 10 年经验的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them has been at your company for 10 years.
zh: 其中一个人在你的公司待了 10 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other person is new to the company.
zh: 另一个人刚来公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you ask both of them to fix a bug or implement a feature or make some architectural decision, who do you think is going to be better at it?
zh: 如果你让这两个人都去修一个 bug、实现一个功能或做某个架构决策，你觉得谁会做得更好?

speaker: Unknown
en: And why do you think that's the case?
zh: 你又为什么觉得是这样?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, they have the same skill set, right?
zh: 我是说,他们有同样的技能组合,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's the one with the context, right?
zh: 但胜出的是有上下文的那个,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Intelligence is not the gap.
zh: 智能不是差距所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's context that's missing.
zh: 缺的是上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the thing that we've been kind of like working on and making available to both people and increasingly their tools to write this code.
zh: 所以这就是我们一直在做的事情，把它做出来并提供给人们，并且越来越多地提供给他们的工具来写这些代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the wins are, you know, very, very quantifiable.
zh: 所以收益是,你知道,非常非常可量化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you been, I guess, like how you get the stuff that's like exists in people's heads that doesn't, isn't even written down, is it about?
zh: 你有没有,我是说,那些存在于人们脑子里、甚至没被写下来的东西,你是怎么获取的,是不是关于……

speaker: Unknown
